project.name: HOMIO
project.type: Global AI Real Estate OS + International Brokerage + SaaS
project.north_star: Generate genuine property demand, acquire verified inventory, protect lead/deal ownership, protect commission, automate operations, and scale internationally.
project.operating_principle: AI automates; governance controls; evidence protects; humans approve irreversible/high-risk actions.

phases.phase_2: Data, Search, Services, Analytics, Security, DevOps & AI Infrastructure

approved.name: Evidence / Consent / Visit / Enquiry Proof Layer

business: Broker can operate internationally with maximum practical automation.
Customer must be attributable to HOMIO/broker even when customer directly contacts builder.
Builder must have verifiable proof that a customer originated through HOMIO.
Customer verification must be one-click/minimal-friction and user-friendly.
Multiple projects and multiple flat options must be tracked without ambiguity.
Commission must be traceable from lead origin through deal and collection.
Genuine leads must be separated from spam/fraud/duplicates.
All important interactions must create auditable evidence.
Preventive governance must stop foreseeable ownership/commission/security errors before they occur.
SEO/data intelligence must continuously support lead generation.
technical: Persist project state outside chat history.
Use IDs and versions for architecture, requirements, decisions, tasks and changes.
Track dependencies and impact before architecture changes.
Keep high-risk actions behind explicit approval gates.
Keep code modular enough to replace components without redesigning the whole system.
The autonomous control center, not conversational improvisation, determines the authoritative next project step.

payload.evidence: Canonical entities have one authoritative source of truth; normalized schema and domain ownership reviewed in T01-T02.
Lead, deal, inventory, trust, fraud, governance and commission relationships are traceable across the schema model.
Tenant isolation and authorization fields were defined in T04 with database-level enforcement requirements.
Primary keys, foreign keys, uniqueness and critical constraints were defined in T03 and T05.
Immutable domain events, audit records, correlation/causation and historical preservation were defined in T06.
Forward-compatible schema migration, versioning, checksums, locking and expand-migrate-contract strategy were defined in T08.
Critical indexes, composite access paths and index governance were defined and reviewed in T05 and T10.
Sensitive-data boundaries, classification, minimization and authorization controls were reviewed in T04 and T10.
Schema boundaries support all approved operating modes without changing the frozen architecture.
Normalization and duplication review found no duplicate source-of-truth or duplicate engine responsibility.
Security, privacy and performance review passed in T10, including isolation, least privilege, query/index and regression controls.

payload.note: Frontend and runtime stack locked: Next.js 16.2 Active LTS, React 19.2, TypeScript 6.0, Node.js 24 LTS, App Router and Turbopack.

Backend and service runtime stack locked: TypeScript, Node.js 24 LTS, Fastify 5.x, REST plus event-driven communication, typed/JSON Schema contracts, Node workers, and modular bounded-service architecture.

Database and data infrastructure locked: PostgreSQL 18.4+ as authoritative system of record, Redis 8.x for cache/ephemeral coordination, S3-compatible object storage for large artifacts, separate search and event infrastructure, and PostgreSQL backup/WAL/PITR recovery strategy.

Event, cache and background execution architecture locked: Apache Kafka for durable domain event streaming, Redis for cache and ephemeral coordination, Node workers for ordinary asynchronous jobs, and Temporal for durable long-running critical workflows with retry, timer and crash-recovery requirements.

Search, vector and AI infrastructure locked: PostgreSQL/PostGIS for structured filtering, Qdrant for hybrid vector/lexical retrieval, HOMIO AI Gateway with OpenAI as managed provider, vLLM as self-hosted fallback, configurable embeddings/reranking, tenant-scoped RAG, model registry, versioned indexing and AI cost/observability controls.

Cloud and container strategy locked: AWS primary cloud, OCI/Docker containers, ECS with Fargate for initial production orchestration, ECR registry, Terraform IaC, private data plane, workload-specific autoscaling, canary deployment, immutable images, rollback, and EKS as a future scale tier.

Observability and security tooling locked: OpenTelemetry and CloudWatch for telemetry, Security Hub/CSPM for centralized security posture and findings, GuardDuty for threat detection and Fargate runtime monitoring, Inspector for vulnerability management, Macie for sensitive-data discovery, WAF, IAM, Secrets Manager, container scanning and structured security/operational alerting.

Cost, scalability and vendor-lock review passed: AWS/ECS-Fargate retained as primary platform, PostgreSQL retained as portable system of record, Kafka/Qdrant/Temporal/Redis retained behind technology abstractions, OpenAI retained behind AI Gateway, managed-vs-self-host decision rules defined, cost observability and migration paths established.

payload.evidence: Every production component has a defined purpose, ownership and deployment responsibility established across T01-T07.
The selected stack supports multi-tenancy, event-driven services, modular deployment and durable workflows.
Search, vector retrieval and AI infrastructure were defined with PostgreSQL/PostGIS, Qdrant, AI Gateway, OpenAI provider abstraction and vLLM fallback.
Security, observability, backup, recovery, IAM, secrets, runtime security and monitoring requirements were defined.
Local, development, staging and production deployment environments with containerized runtime and controlled promotion were defined.
Technology choices, alternatives, rejected options and vendor-lock escape paths were reviewed in T08.
Cost, scaling, autoscaling, workload classes, AI spend and infrastructure cost visibility were defined.
Unnecessary technologies were rejected; Kubernetes, multi-cloud and duplicate databases were not introduced without measured need.

execution_plan.objective: Complete pre-coding architecture, freeze the master blueprint, generate the repository foundation, then execute production coding in controlled dependency order.
execution_plan.selection_rule: The Control Center is the authoritative planner. It selects the next gate from dependencies and completion state. The assistant executes the current gate and must not invent the roadmap.
execution_plan.change_rule: A plan change requires a change request, duplicate/dependency/impact review, and explicit user approval before the authoritative sequence changes.
execution_plan.completion_rule: A gate becomes COMPLETE only when its acceptance criteria are recorded and the Control Center records the state transition.
